messages.subject: MIRT Simulation diagnostics Function
messages.body_plain:
Loving the MIRTCAT Package, thanks for all your work Phil!

I was wondering if anyone has written code for more detailed post-simulation metrics? E.g., stats outputs of performance and rendering visualisation with GGPlot. Ideally it would be great to also be able to subset this by a criterion (when supplied; e.g., item content domains "content_prop"; or participant demographics [although ideally this would not show much difference under non-dif items]).

This is likely all possible using the output already contained within the Mirt Cat object in addition to a few other calculations, however, it would be nice to not reinvent the wheel if much of the code for this post-simulation diagnostics already exists. If not, this chain could provide some ideas / code for future researchers interested in simulation-diagnostics.

Although this could be dreaming, Many of these could also be utilised post-Shiny administration to also diagnose how the CAT went with real participant data.

Some I had in mind were:

Performance metrics such as:
Efficiency
Average Number of Items Administered
Time reduction  / average item reduction
Bias
MSE
RMSE
Pearson Correlation Coef between true theta and Cat estimates, and between CAT estimated and simply taking the mean of all items (e.g., the standard approach using Classical test theory)
Total % who met stop criteria

Error metrics such as:
Mean SE
Min SE
Max SE
Std. Dev. of SE
% < certain thresholds, e.g., % <= 0.30, % <= 0.25,  % <= 0.15

Some Visualisations (each could also have range/sd bar options):
Item number or ID vs Frequency of administration
Theta (X) vs average # of items (Y)
Average Final Ability Estimate vs Simulated θ
Average Standard Error vs Final Ability Estimate
Average Test Information vs Final Ability Estimate

Kind Regards,
    Conal

messages.subject: Communicating uncertainty in empirical reliability
messages.body_plain:
Phil,

I have an applied scenario in which empirical reliability must be reported, even in situations where the sample size is less than ideal. I'd like to demonstrate the hazards of interpreting that coefficient via something like a confidence interval around it, but I'm unsure of the best approach.

could I, in theory, use fscore SEs to compute an upper and lower bound fscore estimate, and then use their variances in computation of empirical reliability?

Christopher

messages.subject: Re: Communicating uncertainty in empirical reliability
messages.body_plain:
I found partial answers to my own question, though there seems to be no agreement in the literature on this from an IRT perspective.

The study below led to the publication of the irtreliability package, though it doesn't work very well, and it's limited to the 3PL and GPCM.

Andersson, B., & Xin, T. (2018). Large sample confidence intervals for item response theory reliability coefficients. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 78(1), 32-45.

Later, they expanded it to other models and multigroup analyses in this paper:

Andersson, B., Luo, H., & Marcq, K. (2022). Reliability coefficients for multiple group item response theory models. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 75(2), 395-410.

In theory, you can use their supplemental code for singlegroup mirt objects, but I can't seem to get that to work either. I've contacted Andersson, who has suggested the code needs some work in both the package and the supplemental code, but do you think these are the best approaches?

Moreover, it seems like a good addition to your package!

messages.subject: Question about running multidimension IRT
messages.body_plain:
Dear Phil,

Two subtests are administered in sequence, each subtes has 20 items, I want to run a 2-dimensional IRT，
When the first subtest was administered, 2-dimensional latent ability was estimated.

the codes below：

library(MASS)
co<-matrix(c(1,0.5,0.5,1),2,2)
theta<-mvrnorm(3000,c(0,0),co)

a1<-c(rlnorm(20,0,0.25),rep(0,20))
a2<-c(rep(0,20),rlnorm(20,0,0.25))
d<-rnorm(40,0,1)
u<-rep(1,40)
g<-rep(0,40)
item<-cbind(a1,a2,d,g,u)
library(mirtCAT)
par<-generate.mirt_object(item,itemtype = "2PL",latent_covariance =co)

library(mirt)
resp<-simdata(a=item[,1:2],d=item[,3],N=3000,itemtype='2PL',Theta = theta)
resp[,21:40] <- NA
ability<-fscores(par, response.pattern = resp,method = "EAP")

What procedure is used to estimate ability[,2]? I am confused about "cor(ability[,2],ability[,2])=1"

Thank you in advance!

Sincerely,
Irene

messages.subject: Re: Question about running multidimension IRT
messages.body_plain:
Hi Irene,

This is a linear artifact, and should be expected. It appears because the second trait has no response information (the resp[,21:40] <- NA line), so all the information comes from the first factor. However, because there is a linear co-relationship between the factors you will ultimately get a perfect correlation due to the defined covariance structure and lack of additional observed information about the second factor. This will be true for any non-zero correlation between the traits, and of course will drop to 0 when the traits are uncorrelated. HTH.

Phil
